anon_readable_tables.note: Aggregate and registry tables carrying a permissive `*_public_read` policy: `for select to anon, authenticated using (true)`. Every one of these publishes figures that already appear in the public GitHub mirror, which is why the posture is accepted rather than closed. Writes are denied everywhere: none of these carries an INSERT, UPDATE or DELETE policy.

anon_readable_views.note: Curated aggregate views in the `api` schema, reachable with the `Accept-Profile: api` header. Each is security_invoker and publishes only the aggregate registry surface already documented for public use.

closed_tables.note: RLS enabled with zero reader policies. Anonymous and authenticated roles have no table privilege on the licensed datasets or the four versioned result bases; the remaining registry and operational logs are also denied every row. The verifier accepts only an RLS-filtered empty array or an explicit SQLSTATE 42501 denial.

closed_views.note: The four current_rp2_* convenience views remain security_invoker but are not part of the anonymous API surface. Migration 20260826210228 revoked their grants and closed the four base tables, avoiding both direct base-table access and a SECURITY DEFINER side door.

provenance_resolution.note: Migration 20260826210228 closes the contradictory versioned-result base policies and views. Migration 20260827073145 retires every current RP2 row and revokes publish_rp2_v3(jsonb) from service_role. Migration 20260828020327 closes direct service-role mutation on those retired tables and future postgres-owned public objects while preserving the six dataset-loader tables. PostgreSQL denies postgres permission to alter supabase_admin defaults; the live audit measured zero public or api relations owned by supabase_admin. The six retained public aggregate tables and four retained curated views remain the documented public surface.

purpose: The access posture of the Supabase project, measured against the live REST endpoint with the anonymous key rather than inferred from policy prose. The 2026-08-24 measurement corrected an earlier claim that anonymous keys read nothing. tests/contract/test_access_posture_matches_documentation.py compares this record with the public policy, and scripts/verify_access_posture.py compares it with the endpoint wherever the anonymous key is available.

writes.note: No role but service_role can write. As of 20260826020000 anon and authenticated hold no INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE/TRUNCATE grant anywhere in `public`, and default privileges were revoked so new tables do not inherit any. RLS was already denying these writes; removing the grants removes the blast radius of a mistaken policy.
